emma (People Ops): Quick Q — an IC asked whether they should do a 401(k) loan vs a hardship withdrawal and what the process/impacts are (tax, match, payroll). tagging @ryan (Payroll) and @alex (Benefits Admin) to confirm vendor steps :wave:
ryan (Payroll): Short answer: if the plan allows loans, loan is usually cleaner (repay via payroll deductions, not taxable while outstanding). hardship is a distribution — taxable and possibly 10% early penalty for <59½. Need vendor paperwork either way. when do they need the cash? that affects timing.
alex (Benefits Admin): Correct. Our plan with Echo401k supports loans and hardship distributions. Differences to flag:
• Loan: up to 50% of vested balance, cap $50k (federal rules). repaid via payroll-withholding (post-tax) plus interest paid to participant. no immediate tax if repaid on schedule.
• Hardship distribution: eligible only for certain reasons (medical, purchase of primary residence, etc.). distribution is taxable and may incur 10% penalty if early. can suspend loans/restrictions vary by plan.
jamal: do employer match contributions stop if you take a hardship?
alex (Benefits Admin): Employer match continues based on contributions going forward. However, if you take a distribution and drop below certain vesting thresholds (rare), that could affect vested match. For practical purposes, your future contributions still get matched per plan.
ryan (Payroll): Process/ops notes:
1) Employee fills vendor loan or hardship form on Echo401k portal (link: https://portal.echo401k.example/requests) or uses the paper form if preferred.
2) For loans: choose repayment schedule (usually 1–5 years; 15 years for primary residence). vendor will send a loan approval notice with a payroll deduction code.
3) For hardship: vendor processes distribution, sends taxable amount and code for payroll tax withholding.
4) Deadline: submit paperwork before payroll cutoff for the pay period when repayment/withholding should start. if missed, first deduction may be delayed.
ryan (Payroll): payroll folks — please route loan deductions under code `401K_LOAN` and hardship withholding under `401K_DIST_TAX`. we need vendor confirmation email attached to the payroll ticket.
alex (Benefits Admin): I'll confirm exact forms. Quick checklist for the employee:
- Confirm eligibility on Echo portal (screenshot helpful)
- Complete loan vs hardship form on portal
- Pick repayment schedule (if loan)
- Forward vendor approval email to payroll@redwood.example with subject: "401k loan/distribution — [name]" by payroll cutoff
- Expect first deduction the following pay after vendor notify + payroll processing
benefits-bot: New doc uploaded: Echo401k loan & hardship quick guide (pdf) — https://s3.example/echo401k-quickguide.pdf :page_facing_up:
emma (People Ops): thanks alex + ryan. i'll send a short blurb to the #benefits-faq with the link and the payroll codes. jamal — if you want, DM me the use-case and i can help pick loan vs hardship. :thumbsup:
jamal: thanks — will DM. appreciate the clarity! :pray:
